discussion_comments.comment_body:
Fixed in `395a8ff`. The single-required-key-with-default branch (Bedrock's only required key, `AWS_REGION`, is defaulted) short-circuited on whether that key was explicitly set and ignored the secret. It now also reports configured when any secret key holds a real value, so a Bedrock setup using `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` with the region resolved from an AWS profile or `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` is offered in the picker. I factored the secret check into a shared `any_secret_configured` helper so this branch and the all-defaulted-required-keys branch can't drift again.

This doesn't reopen the original default-only Bedrock case: a fresh install has neither an explicit `AWS_REGION` nor a bearer token, so Bedrock stays excluded until a real credential is present.

Real gap, but it belongs in the per-provider follow-up (#9822) rather than this metadata predicate. The usable credential for OAuth-backed providers lives in their token cache, which only `inventory_configured()` (e.g. `ChatGptCodexProvider`'s `TokenCache::new().load().is_some()`) can see. The shared `check_provider_configured` works from `ProviderMetadata` keys and structurally can't observe a provider's token cache. Gating the picker on each registry entry's `inventory_configured()` is the fix, and it closes this together with the other provider-specific cases.

Real, but it's the same blind spot as the other provider-specific cases and shouldn't be patched in this predicate. `AWS_PROFILE` is a non-required key defaulting to `default`, and it's commonly set in a developer's shell for unrelated AWS CLI use, so gating Bedrock on it would surface the provider for anyone who has AWS configured at all, reintroducing the fresh-install false positive the strict check was added to prevent. Only `BedrockProvider::from_env` (which resolves the region from the profile/SDK chain) can tell a Bedrock-capable setup from generic AWS config. Folding into the per-provider `inventory_configured()` work in #9822.

Fixed in 008c1e7b8.

Both `resolve_provider_model_info` and `get_provider_models` were pre-filling `context_limit` with catalog and/or canonical values before calling `goose::providers::create`. This set a positive value that caused `normalize_model_config` to skip the `known_models` override.

**Fix:** Removed all pre-fills (`with_catalog_provider_fallback` and `with_canonical_limits`) from both endpoints. Now `ModelConfig::new(model)` is passed directly to `create`, and `normalize_model_config` handles the full chain: known_models → catalog → canonical. The registry-normalized config from `provider.get_model_config()` is used as the authoritative source for the returned `ModelInfo`.

Valid concern but this is pre-existing behavior — set_active_provider marks configured: true on every call, which is the same semantics as the old flat-key {name}_configured = true write. OAuth providers go through a separate auth flow that validates credentials before calling set_active_provider; you can't reach set_active_provider for an OAuth provider without completing that flow first. The check_provider_configured guard (per P1 "Stop short-circuiting configured checks") now re-validates required API keys for non-OAuth providers regardless of the configured flag, so a stale configured: true on a provider with missing keys is caught at readiness check time. No change needed in this PR — tightening the semantics of configured for OAuth providers would be a separate concern.

Valid observation. When GOOSE_PROVIDER is set as an environment variable, get_goose_provider() returns the env value, so a GOOSE_MODEL upsert would persist the model under the env-overridden provider rather than the configured active_provider. In practice this is a narrow edge case — env overrides are used for CI/testing, not interactive UI sessions where model switching happens. However, the fix is straightforward: use get_active_provider() with an env-skip variant or read active_provider directly from config. I'll note this as a follow-up improvement outside this PR's scope since the current behavior matches pre-structured-config semantics (the old code also read GOOSE_PROVIDER through get_param which checks env first).
